Notice that $\Phi_{\mu}(\wvx+\vv)=\sum_{i\in \mathrm{supp}(\wvx)}\phi_{\mu}(\wvx_i+\vv_i)+\sum_{i\notin \mathrm{supp}(\wvx)}\phi_{\mu}(\wvx_i+\vv_i)$ with  the second term being nonnegative, the lemma holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract/introduction claim that the local-optimality result lets exact and robust recovery theories (which concern global minimizers and uniqueness) be 'directly extended' to the TH penalty. What Theorem TH:s-sparse actually proves is that every feasible vector whose nonzero entries exceed mu in magnitude is a local minimizer of Phi_mu over S, regardless of whether it is recoverable by any other penalty; Phi_mu is locally s + sum v_i^2/mu^2 there. This says nothing about global optimality, uniqueness, or error bounds, and no argument in the paper connects local optimality to exact/robust recovery guarantees.

failure_location.quote: This property allows the exact and robust recovery theories developed for other penalty regularization functions to be directly extended to the truncated Huber function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim that recovery theories extend to the TH penalty, or restate it as the local-optimality property actually proved in Theorem TH:s-sparse.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised transfer of exact/robust recovery theory to the TH model is unsupported; only the (much weaker, essentially universal) local-optimality property is established.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that Theorem TH:s-sparse transfers exact/robust recovery theory to the TH penalty
issues.why_classification: The correction removes an advertised theoretical guarantee (extension of exact/robust recovery theory) that nothing in the paper supports; no other result depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The only tool used to identify the limit is Theorem linearoptcond, whose sufficiency direction certifies a local minimizer (the sufficiency proof only shows Phi(x+v) >= Phi(x) for ||v||_inf <= rho). The BCD iteration on the nonconvex problem cannot guarantee a global minimizer, and nothing in the proof rules out convergence to a non-global local minimizer; the paper's own experiments report 'algorithm failures' where Phi(x_bar) < Phi(x_hat). The statement 'the minimizer' is therefore stronger than what is proved.

issues.overall_effect: The finite-step convergence guarantee of the noise-free BCD scheme holds only for a stationary point that is a local minimizer, not for the global solution of (constrain_model).
issues.title: Theorem covgergalg1 claims convergence to 'the minimizer' but the argument yields at most a local minimizer

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem linearoptcond requires |x_i| != mu for all i. The limit/fixed point of the BCD scheme satisfies only the stationarity system and omega = H_mu(x); nothing prevents a fixed point with some |x_i| = mu on I_2 (x_{I_2} is a specific linear image of y, and H_mu assigns omega_i = 0 at |x_i| = mu). At such a point Theorem linearoptcond is not applicable, and by the proof of Theorem THdifferentiable_refined the point is not a local minimizer at all, so the algorithm can stall at a non-minimizer.

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality Q(x^1, omega^0) <= Q(x^0, omega^0) holds only if x^0 is feasible (A x^0 = b), since x^1 minimizes Q(., omega^0) over the feasible set. The theorem assumes only Q(x^0, omega^0) < spark(A). If x^0 is infeasible, ||omega^1||_0 <= Q(x^1, omega^0) need not be < spark(A), so the subsequent x-update matrices may be singular and the finite-convergence argument collapses.

issues.overall_effect: Theorem covgergalg1 is not guaranteed for infeasible initial points; the proof's monotone chain is unjustified at its first step.
issues.title: Descent chain in Theorem covgergalg1 requires feasibility of the initial point, which is not assumed
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis on the initialization repairs the argument with no loss of the stated conclusion.
